templates.name: Addition/similarity: a further item of the same kind
Contrast: established view or appearance, then a finding that breaks it
Contrast: positive claim, then a limiting fact about the same subject
Cause/effect: condition, principle or evidence, then its consequence
Cause/effect: need or judgment, then the action it motivates
Concession: grant, then the main claim resumes (but / Still)
Emphasis: stronger same-direction fact (content-contrast trap at hard)
Purpose and aptness: goal then deliberate act, or a fitting echo
Specification/restatement: exact content or plain rewording
Sequence/time: next step, earlier or later event, end of a long effort
Culmination, alternative and place (ultimately, alternatively, there)
Example: general claim, then one named instance

items.passage: Linguists classify Hawai‘i Creole English, known locally as Pidgin, as an independent language, and since 2015 the US Census Bureau has listed it among the languages spoken in American homes. ______ most of Pidgin’s vocabulary is derived from English. But its grammar is distinctive: ongoing actions are signaled with the marker “stay,” a construction absent from standard English.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence claims that Pidgin is a language in its own right. The blank sentence admits a fact that seems to weaken that claim: most of its vocabulary comes from English. The next sentence turns back with “But,” showing that Pidgin’s grammar is distinctive. “Granted” introduces a point the writer concedes before returning to the main claim.

A.why_wrong: “Moreover” would add a further reason to treat Pidgin as a separate language, but borrowing most of its words from English is a reason to doubt that, which is why the next sentence has to answer it with “But.”

C.why_wrong: An English-based vocabulary is not an example of Pidgin being a language in its own right; it is a point against that view.

D.why_wrong: Being classified as a language and listed by the Census Bureau does not cause Pidgin’s vocabulary to come from English.

items.notes: Grant then turn, the turn opened by But in the next sentence (3.17 and 3.19 shape), keyed Granted. K1 has no band-7 official items (spec/rw/band7/transitions.md section 5), so this is written as a strong band 6 and band_target is 6, not the 7 the plan asked for. Trap: Moreover, for a reader who takes the blank sentence as more description of Pidgin. No In fact or Indeed and no contrast word beside the concession key. Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

band7.why: K1 has no band-7 official items, so it stays a strong band 6: grant then But as in f5959727 (Of course ... Still), with additive, example and cause decoys and no contrast decoy.

items.passage: Indian sandalwood, prized for its fragrant heartwood, grows readily in the mixed dry forests of southern India, yet seedlings planted in stands of sandalwood alone have often withered. The tree is a root hemiparasite; ______ it produces its own sugars through photosynthesis but draws much of its water and mineral nutrients from the roots of neighboring plants.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The clause before the blank names a technical category: sandalwood is a root hemiparasite. The clause after it says the same thing in plain terms: the tree makes its own sugars but takes water and minerals from other plants’ roots, which is what being a partial parasite of roots means. “That is” signals this rewording.

A.why_wrong: Making its own sugars can look like a contrast with being a parasite, but a hemiparasite is only partly parasitic. The clause after the blank explains what the term means; it does not hold true in spite of it.

B.why_wrong: The clause after the blank is not a second, separate fact about the tree; it spells out the meaning of “root hemiparasite.”

C.why_wrong: The clause after the blank is not one instance of hemiparasitism among others; it describes what the term means for sandalwood as a whole.

items.notes: Restatement keyed that is after a semicolon. Band-7 setting: surface contrast inside B (although its leaves make sugars ... it draws ... from neighbors) next to a parasite label, with nevertheless as the false-opposition decoy, plus a yet in the prior sentence; the term is glossed only by B, so in addition pulls a reader who does not see B as the gloss. No cause decoy (B is the definition, so a cause word could be read as defensible). Not the popular-picture / study-found frame of the three existing more-often items. Section 6 checks (spec/rw/band7/transitions.md): key outside the core 13, no obvious decoys, surface-contrast proxy passes (yet in the sentence before the blank), chars per word 5.36. Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation. Review 2026-10-20: B reordered so the main clause right after the blank (produces its own sugars) reads as a contrast with parasite; the old although made nevertheless read awkwardly, an easy kill.
band7_moves: surface contrast with a non-adversative key (although inside B, parasite label in A)
adversative yet in the sentence before the blank

fixes: reordered the clause after the blank (produces its own sugars ... but draws ...) so nevertheless is a live lure instead of an awkward fit after although; why_wrong for A updated

band7.why: Hardened (the nevertheless lure now meets a self-sufficient-sounding clause right after the blank), but a technical term followed by its gloss is the band-6 That is pattern of e3edc138; S1 reaches band 7 only in the more-often frame of d3b7d7a3, already used by three bank items.

items.passage: German instrument maker Heinrich Band began selling the bandoneon, a type of concertina, in the 1840s, and early on it was promoted partly as an inexpensive substitute for the organ in modest rural churches. ______ the instrument’s fame emerged from a very different setting: carried to Buenos Aires by European immigrants, it became the defining sound of Argentine tango.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence gives the bandoneon’s beginnings as a cheap stand-in for a church organ. The blank sentence gives where the instrument ended up and what it is now known for: the sound of tango in Buenos Aires. “Ultimately” signals this final outcome, reached after the instrument’s early use.

B.why_wrong: Being sold as a substitute for a church organ did not cause the bandoneon to become famous in tango; the sentence after the blank stresses that its fame came from a very different setting.

C.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not add a further point about the bandoneon’s use in churches; it tells where the instrument ended up.

D.why_wrong: Tango is not an example of the bandoneon being used in place of an organ in small churches.

items.notes: Culmination keyed Ultimately: an original purpose in A, the lasting outcome in B (3.4 shape, an initial impression then what finally counts). A stays on the original purpose, so the cause decoy fails because A does not produce B. No contrast word offered, since B itself turns against A. Band 6 by plan. Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

band7.why: Band 6 by plan: an early purpose, then where the fame finally came from, as in 6e0c60da; hence, moreover and for example are the U1 recipe decoys, and very different setting kills the cause decoy.

items.passage: Dawn redwoods, conifers indigenous to central China, turn a coppery orange each autumn and then shed all their needles, leaving their branches bare until spring. Among cone-bearing trees, such seasonal needle loss is exceptional; ______ the vast majority of conifers, including pines, spruces, and firs, retain their needles throughout the winter and replace them only gradually.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The clause before the blank says that shedding needles each autumn, as dawn redwoods do, is unusual among cone-bearing trees. The clause after it backs up and sharpens that claim: the vast majority of conifers keep their needles all winter. “Indeed” signals this stronger statement in the same direction.

A.why_wrong: Conifers that keep their needles behave the opposite way from dawn redwoods, but that is the evidence that needle loss is unusual, not something true in spite of it.

B.why_wrong: “That said” would introduce a point that qualifies the claim that seasonal needle loss is unusual, but most conifers keeping their needles all winter makes that claim stronger, not weaker.

D.why_wrong: The habit of most conifers is not a separate, further point; it is the reason that needle loss counts as unusual among cone-bearing trees.

items.notes: Band-7 M1 frame of 47e238be and a266d876 (an unusual case, then the majority with the opposite value), built without their outlier wording. Surface contrast: conifers that keep their needles read against dawn redwoods that shed theirs, so nevertheless and that said (synonym pair, allowed at band 7) pull a hurried reader; in addition pulls a reader who takes B as one more fact. Review 2026-10-20: rewritten from a draft whose B (the small wild population) only supported the clause before it, so the adversative decoys had nothing to grab. Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.
band7_moves: surface contrast with a non-adversative key (shed vs keep needles)
two false-opposition decoys (synonym pair) plus an additive decoy

fixes: rebuilt passage and options on the band-7 M1 frame (dawn redwoods shed their needles, most conifers keep theirs); old B only supported the clause before it, so the draft read band 6; explanation, distractors and notes rewritten
unusual changed to exceptional so the hard tier meets the long-word floor in check_rw

band7.why: Rebuilt on the 47e238be and a266d876 mechanism: B describes the majority with the opposite habit, so its surface points to contrast while it proves the claim; key indeed outside the core 13, adversative synonym pair plus an additive decoy, blank after a semicolon, 5.51 chars per word.

items.passage: Tuvan throat singers produce two pitches simultaneously: a sustained low drone and, floating above it, a melody of overtones. In the style called sygyt, those overtones resonate as a piercing, flutelike whistle; in kargyraa, ______ the drone itself descends dramatically, and the singer generates a deep, rumbling growl.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text describes two styles of throat singing. In sygyt the overtones make a piercing whistle, while in kargyraa the drone descends and the singer growls. “By contrast” signals that the second style has the opposite quality from the first.

A.why_wrong: Kargyraa is not an example of the high, whistling sygyt style; it is a different style with the opposite sound.

B.why_wrong: “Similarly” would mean kargyraa sounds like sygyt, but a deep growl is the opposite of a piercing whistle.

D.why_wrong: The high whistle of sygyt does not cause the drone in kargyraa to drop low; the two are separate styles.

items.notes: Two subjects, opposite values, blank after an introductory phrase in the second clause of a semicolon sentence (2.4 position). Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: In 1872, physicist William Thomson (later Lord Kelvin) designed a machine that predicted tides by adding together ten constituents, the regular rhythms, set by the Moon and Sun, that combine to produce a tide. A machine built for the US Coast and Geodetic Survey in the 1910s, ______ combined thirty-seven constituents.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence says Thomson’s machine added together ten constituents. The second says a later machine combined thirty-seven. “By comparison” signals that the second machine is being measured against the first on the same feature, the number of constituents.

B.why_wrong: The second sentence does not reword the description of Thomson’s machine; it describes a different machine with a different number of constituents.

C.why_wrong: The 1910s machine is not an instance of Thomson’s machine or of any general claim in the first sentence; it is a second machine set beside the first.

D.why_wrong: Thomson’s machine summing ten constituents did not cause the later machine to sum thirty-seven; the text gives no such link.

items.notes: Two subjects compared on a number (by comparison, as in 1.14), placed as an interrupter after a long subject noun phrase. No similarity word offered, since both machines add constituents. Later machine is the US Coast and Geodetic Survey Tide Predicting Machine No. 2 (37 constituents, in use from about 1912). Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: Indian chemist Asima Chatterjee devoted much of her career to investigating the medicinal compounds found in plants. From the aquatic fern Marsilea minuta, she developed Ayush-56, an anticonvulsant drug used to treat epilepsy. ______ her research on alkaloids extracted from the Madagascar periwinkle advanced the study of compounds now used in cancer chemotherapy.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text says Chatterjee studied medicinal compounds in plants and gives one result: a drug for epilepsy made from a fern. The blank sentence gives a second, separate contribution: her research on periwinkle alkaloids used against cancer. “Additionally” signals this further item of the same kind.

A.why_wrong: Her periwinkle research does not hold true in spite of her work on the epilepsy drug; the two contributions point the same way.

B.why_wrong: Developing a drug from a fern did not cause her research on periwinkle alkaloids; they are two separate lines of work.

C.why_wrong: “Instead” would mean the periwinkle research replaced the work on Ayush-56, but the text presents both as parts of her career.

items.notes: Two contributions by one person (2.11 shape). No example decoy, because the blank sentence could be read as an instance of the first sentence; no similarity decoy beside an addition key. Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: Among the Mbuti people of Congo’s Ituri Forest, men produce barkcloth from the inner bark of trees, and women decorate it with intricate designs painted in a plant-based dye. ______ the women combine juice extracted from the fruit of a gardenia shrub with powdered charcoal, applying the mixture with twigs or their fingertips.

items.explanation: The first sentence says only that the women paint designs with a plant-based dye. The blank sentence gives the exact details of that dye and how it is applied: gardenia juice combined with powdered charcoal, applied with twigs or fingertips. “Specifically” signals this more precise account of the same point.

C.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not describe a similar, separate activity; it describes the same painting in more detail.

D.why_wrong: Painting with a plant dye is not a reason the women mix gardenia juice with charcoal; the mixing is simply what that painting consists of.

items.passage: In the early 2010s, management researchers studying how entrepreneurs in India solve problems on limited budgets drew attention to jugaad—______ improvising an inexpensive, makeshift solution from whatever materials happen to be available. items.passage: Cecropia trees of tropical America shelter colonies of Azteca ants in their hollow stems and supply them with nutritious food bodies produced at the bases of the leaf stalks. In return, the ants attack herbivorous insects and sever climbing vines. ______ Cecropia trees occupied by ants generally sustain far less damage to their foliage than unoccupied trees.

items.explanation: The text explains that the ants living in Cecropia trees attack plant-eating insects and cut away climbing vines. The blank sentence gives the result of that protection: trees with ants suffer much less leaf damage than trees without them. “Consequently” signals this result.

B.why_wrong: “Instead” would mean the reduced leaf damage replaces the ants’ defense, but it follows from that defense.

C.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not describe a similar, separate case; it states the outcome of the ants’ behavior described just before it.

items.passage: In 2011, the World Organisation for Animal Health declared that rinderpest, a viral disease that had devastated herds of cattle, buffalo, and other hoofed animals across Africa, Asia, and Europe, had been eradicated after a decades-long international campaign. ______ only one disease, smallpox, had ever been eliminated through deliberate human effort.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence reports that rinderpest was declared eradicated in 2011. The blank sentence describes the situation before that declaration: up to then, smallpox was the only disease ever eliminated by human effort. “Previously” signals that the blank sentence refers to an earlier time.

A.why_wrong: The eradication of rinderpest did not cause smallpox to be the only disease eliminated; that was the situation before 2011.

C.why_wrong: Smallpox is not an example of rinderpest’s eradication; it is a different disease, and the sentence is about the record before 2011.

D.why_wrong: The sentence does not describe a similar event; it states that before 2011 only one disease had ever been eliminated, which no longer held once rinderpest was eradicated.

items.passage: After black rats reached Lord Howe Island, east of mainland Australia, in 1918, the island’s large, flightless stick insect disappeared and was presumed extinct. In 2001, ______ researchers climbing Ball’s Pyramid, a steep volcanic sea stack more than 20 kilometers from the island, discovered a small population of the insects sheltering beneath a single shrub.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence says the stick insect was presumed extinct after rats arrived on its island. The second sentence reports a finding that contradicts that belief: in 2001, researchers found a small population on a nearby sea stack. “However” signals this contrast.

A.why_wrong: The insect being presumed extinct did not cause the discovery of a surviving population; the discovery overturned that belief.

B.why_wrong: The discovery on Ball’s Pyramid is not an example of the insect disappearing; it shows that the insect had survived.

C.why_wrong: The discovery does not add a further point in support of the insect’s extinction; it contradicts it.

items.notes: Belief then finding, the blank after the introductory phrase In 2001 (2.1 position, lowercase options). Researchers left unnamed. Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: When Korean scholar-official Kim Man-jung was banished to a remote province in 1687, he hoped to spare his widowed mother the loneliness of his absence. ______ according to a long-standing account, he composed The Cloud Dream of the Nine, a novel of romance and adventure, expressly for her to read while he was in exile.

items.explanation: The first sentence states Kim Man-jung’s goal: to keep his mother from being lonely while he was in exile. The blank sentence describes what he did to serve that goal: he wrote a novel for her to read. “To that end” signals an action taken to achieve a stated aim.

A.why_wrong: Writing a novel for his mother does not contrast with his wish to spare her loneliness; it carries that wish out.

B.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not reword his hope; it describes a separate action he took because of it.

D.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not describe a similar, separate case; it tells what Kim Man-jung himself did to achieve his goal.

items.notes: Goal then deliberate act, keyed To that end (3.15 shape at medium). No cause decoy beside a purpose key. items.passage: Puerto Rican writer Julia de Burgos earned lasting acclaim for her poetry, including “Río Grande de Loíza,” a tribute to the river that flowed past her childhood home. ______ she worked as a journalist during the 1940s, contributing articles to Pueblos Hispanos, a Spanish-language weekly newspaper published in New York City.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence describes the work that earned de Burgos lasting acclaim, her poetry. The blank sentence adds a second kind of work she did: journalism for a New York newspaper. “In addition” signals this further, separate point.

B.why_wrong: Her journalism does not contradict the claim that her poetry earned her acclaim; it is another activity.

C.why_wrong: Writing for a newspaper is not a rewording of writing poetry; it is a different kind of work.

D.why_wrong: The blank sentence describes work she did in the 1940s, not something happening today.

items.notes: Two kinds of work by one writer. Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: Darwin’s frogs, amphibians of Chilean and Argentine forests, are named for Charles Darwin, who collected specimens during the Beagle’s voyage. Males of the species are unusually devoted parents. ______ a male carries his developing offspring inside his vocal sac for weeks, until they emerge from his mouth as froglets.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence before the blank says male Darwin’s frogs are unusually devoted parents. The blank sentence gives a striking fact that strengthens that claim: a male carries his young inside his vocal sac for weeks. “In fact” signals this stronger support.

A.why_wrong: Carrying the young for weeks does not happen in spite of the males being devoted parents; it shows how devoted they are.

C.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not describe something that happened before the males’ parenting; it describes that parenting.

D.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not compare the males with anything else; it adds a fact about the same frogs.

items.notes: Claim, then a stronger same-direction fact (1.6 shape). No example decoy, since the blank sentence could be read as an instance of devotion.
